extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers, conference organizers, and researchers studying peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical analysis of the ICLR conference review process (2017–2020) to quantify reproducibility/randomness, measure correlation between review scores and later paper impact, detect institutional and gender bias, and produce recommendations for organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / randomness in review scores
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper analyzes how consistent numeric reviewer scores are across reviews and over time; this is presented as a measurable property indicating whether scores reliably reflect paper quality or contain substantial randomness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / randomness in acceptance decisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study measures how reproducible accept/reject outcomes are (i.e., how much acceptance decisions vary due to randomness rather than stable signals of quality), treating acceptance consistency as a criterion for a trustworthy review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation between review scores and paper impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether scores correlate with paper impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper evaluates predictive validity: do higher review scores correspond to greater subsequent impact (e.g., citations)? This metric assesses whether score-based selection aligns with downstream measures of value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional bias in accept/reject decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and quantify institutional bias in acceptance decisions, controlling for paper quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors report 'strong institutional bias in accept/reject decisions, even after controlling for paper quality.' As an evaluative criterion, this examines whether authors' institutional affiliations systematically influence outcomes beyond merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender gap in scores, acceptance, and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure gender-related disparities: female authors receiving lower scores, lower acceptance rates, and fewer citations per paper than male counterparts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper finds evidence for a gender gap across multiple dimensions (scores, acceptance rates, citations). This criterion assesses fairness with respect to author gender and its relation to both review outcomes and subsequent impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for future conference organizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide actionable recommendations to improve conference review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work concludes with recommendations for future conference organizers aimed at addressing identified problems (randomness, lack of reproducibility, institutional and gender bias). Guidance includes proposing reforms that conference organizers can adopt, though the abstract only states their existence rather than enumerating them in the provided text.
